What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#11 ("Version 1 review: confirm the text; baselines not run (cluster HT, GNN)") by `experiment-repo`  > **Unnormalised Horvitz-Thompson columns for the cluster designs: done.** (GNN cells still running; P6/P7 running.)
  > 
  > What was computed: `scripts/run_ht.py` reran the 22 cluster runs with the same assignments and graph draws as the delivered runs (`check_rerun.py`: every array of the original runs, i.e. exposures, tau-hat, SE, SD, is reproduced exactly, 22 of 22 runs) and added the exposure estimators with exposure probabilities of the cluster design computed by Monte Carlo (M = 1000, floor 1e-4): ht75 / ht100 (unnormalised) next to hajek75 / hajek100 (self-normalised). `analysis/make_ht.py` -> `cluster_ht_cells.csv`. Population: 22 cluster runs x mechanisms (a)-(f) x s in {0.25,0.5,0.75}... precisely the cells with s>0 at noise multiple 0.5: 132 cells (hajek100 is undefined in too many draws in 18 of them and is left out of its own median: 114 cells). Six cluster runs at resolution 0.3 have no cells: Louvain returned one cluster on graph draw 0 (also in the original runs; recorded as `.degenerate.json`), so they are not in any cluster table.
  > 
  > Median RMSE ratio to the Chin regression under the same cluster design (cells with s>0), by estimator, and the share of cells where it has the smaller RMSE:
  > 
  > | estimator | median ratio to regression | beats regression | beats cluster DM |
  > |---|---|---|---|
  > | regression | 1 | - | 74% |
  > | cluster DM | 1.63 | 26% | - |
  > | hajek75 (the one in the paper) | 1.37 | 32% | 81% |
  > | hajek100 | 3.63 | 6% | 22% |
  > | ht75 | 5.25 | 0% | 0% |
  > | ht100 | 14.4 | 0% | 0% |
  > 
  > By mechanism (median ratio to the regression): hajek75 is 1.30-1.63 on (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) and 0.50 on the threshold mechanism (d); DM is 0.55 on (d). ht75 is 2.98-6.43 and ht100 13.2-24.9 everywhere. So: the unnormalised forms are never better than the regression or than cluster DM in any cell; the Hájek choice in the paper is the favourable one for the baseline, not the unfavourable one, and the paper can say so. On (d) under cluster designs the exposure estimator (Hájek 0.75) beats the regression, as DM does; this is the cluster-design counterpart of the result that the regression fails on (d).
  > 
  > Text consequences (yours): design.tex line 15 / method.tex line 8 can say the cluster designs use the Hájek form and that the unnormalised HT forms were run on the 22 cluster runs and are worse (table above; file `results/cluster_ht_cells.csv` follows with the next export together with the GNN table). The GNN sentences in design.tex and discussion.tex stay as they are until the GNN table lands; I will post the numbers here.
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#11 ("Version 1 review: confirm the text; baselines not run (cluster HT, GNN)") by `experiment-repo`  > Two corrections to the previous comment. (1) The cells are s = 0.5 only (the HT rerun kept s in {0, 0.5}): 22 runs x 6 mechanisms = 132 cells with s>0, not the three-share grid. (2) hajek100 has 114 of the 132 cells because in the other 18 it is undefined in every draw (no unit is exposed at the full-neighbourhood threshold), not 'in too many draws'; the other columns are defined in all 132 cells (hajek75 in 99% of draws).
